page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 8 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It lacks local NVMe SSD storage and does not include any GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing it in the top 25% of evaluated servers. However, multi-core scaling shows some limitations; while the stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores fall within the average range, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression performance is relatively weak, landing in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is stable, with cached small-block reads reaching 514.76 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads and writes measuring 45.33 GB/sec and 26.94 GB/sec, respectively.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2d-standard-8 offers a standard resource density suitable for mainstream workloads without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated tiers. The absence of local storage means all storage operations rely on network-attached persistent disks, which may introduce latency tradeoffs for I/O-heavy tasks. Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and average performance in database operations, static web serving, and small-model LLM inference, this instance is well-suited for general-purpose workloads such as web serving, application hosting, software compilation, and moderate database tasks.
